During the 16 Days of Activism, Kisumu County established a Moot Court for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV)—a strategic effort aimed at elevating cases that often go unnoticed or are derailed through systemic corruption, case mismanagement, or file disappearance. This was a direct outcome of sustained advocacy by WGG East Africa partners, particularly through the “Feminist Demands to End Violence Against Women and Girls” campaign. The Moot Court serves as both a symbolic and practical tool for accountability, reflecting the success of WGG’s ongoing work. 2. WGG Kenya partners added their voice in asking for an inclusive Cabinet: Kenya’s cabinet must ensure inclusion of women with disabilities.Three major collective advocacy initiatives were conducted, including structured policy dialogues in Nairobi and Mombasa and a national convening of women with disabilities. These spaces generated evidence-based policy recommendations on disability-inclusive GBV response, political participation, and institutional accountability .
